about: The eval harness: it asks a synthetic person's questions of one model twice, once reaching her pod only through `cascade-mcp` (the pod arm) and once reading every download (the records arm), checks each answer by program, has blind judges grade the rest against a key written before any run, and writes the results and a report. It is run on demand by `cascade-evals`; no app calls it.

glossary.definition: what a reply says the records lack: the codes and words a record of it would carry (`match`), what was looked through (`coverage`), and the tool call (`query`) or the files (`sources`) that looked.
here, the reply a subject writes to one question, saved as `<question>.json` in the job's folder under the run's `answers/`.
one of the two ways a model is given a person's records: the pod arm or the records arm.
of an absence, borne out by what was looked through; an absence that is not comes back with `backed: false` and a `reason`.
of a point in an answer, matching no key item; a judge gives each a verdict of its own: fair, true but not planted, speculative, or contradicted by the records.
the most tokens and dollars a config lets a run spend; a job that would pass it is not started.
a synthetic person the harness asks about: her downloads, her questions in sessions, and the key, in a folder of `cases/`.
one copy of a repository on disk; a job can be reused from a run made in another checkout, such as a worktree.
the `claude -p` process the runner starts for one job.
where a fact points (`cite`): a view entry, a FHIR resource in a download, or a line of one. In a reply about downloads it also gives, field by field, what the fact says the record there holds.
the whole pod as tab-separated text, which the `ask` tool returns a part at a time when called with `format: "compact"`; each line is one row of a view, its cells separated by tabs.
a file of `configs/` that says which cases, models, repeats and judges a run has, and its cap; `smoke`, `standard` and `full` are the tiers.
the part of the report that shows one answer as a person could hand it to a doctor: the question, the short answer, each dated fact with its source.
a file of a person's records as a hospital's server or portal gave it, before any import: FHIR resources in JSON, or a C-CDA document.
one record an item rests on: what the model says of it, and where it is.
a published list of the versions of reference tables, which an app reads to find newer ones.
Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources: HL7's standard for health records as JSON.
one kind of thing a record says: its `value`, `unit`, `status`, `code`, `name` or `id`, a date (`date`, `start`, `end`, `recorded`), or its text (`text`, from which a `quote` is taken).
to return a job a child left unfinished to `pending`, with what the child wrote removed, so the next `--go` runs it again from the start.
the moment `ask` gives a session its next question; also said of a job the runner has given to a child.

a compact read's short name for a view entry: a letter for its view, then the first eight or more hexadecimal digits of the view entry's name, such as `L41e35923`. `ask` takes a list of them in `entries` to return only those view entries' rows.
a digest of everything a session's answers depend on; a recorded session with the same hash is reused, not run again.
one case, model and repeat, with both arms' sessions and their judging: the unit the report counts.
one point of a reply, with what it rests on.
one unit of work the runner hands out: a subject's session on one arm, or one judge's sitting.
a model that grades both arms' answers against the key without being told which arm wrote which.
what a case's author wrote, before any run, that a good answer to each question finds: `key.json` for programs and `key.md` for the judges.
one thing the key expects of one question: a fact or an absence to find, a planted gap to raise, or a trap to avoid.
the names, A and B, under which a packet shows the two arms' answers, in an order drawn for each judge's sitting.
a language model that an app lets answer a person's questions about their records.
the one file a judge reads: the questions, both arms' blinded answers under letters, and the key's prose.
the lines of a download a citation points at, as the harness read them, at most `PASSAGE_CAP` characters.
a run whose config names a commit for each repository the pod arm depends on; the runtime of those commits builds the pods and serves them.
a run's `plan.json`: its config, cases and jobs, each job with its status.
one person's records, and what that person has said about them, kept as files in one folder.
the arm in which the model reaches the person's pod only through `cascade-mcp`'s tools.
a page of the report that holds every doctor card of one arm of one run, laid out for paper.
a digest of every part of an arm's prompt; it is one of a session's inputs.
of a view entry, what the pod's own files say it came from: its records, each record's versions, and the documents those were read from.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
the arm in which the model is given every download as a file and reads them itself.
public code lists, such as RxNorm for medicines, that tell a runtime when two codes mean one thing.
a model's answer to a person's question about their records, as JSON.
the form a reply must take: an `answer`, a `short` form of it, and `items`. `replySchema` is its JSON Schema, and `replyErrors()` lists where a reply departs from it.
one record in FHIR, named by its type and its id, such as `Observation/ldl-1`.
one execution of a config, in a folder of `runs/`: its plan, prompts, answers, verdicts and, once finished, `results.json` and the report.
the function that replaces, with `[record]`, text only one arm writes: a resource reference, a file name with a line, a handle, an IRI.
one chat: the questions a case asks in it, asked in order of one model on one arm. A subject's job is one session.
the reference tables as the package carries them, which a new app uses until it has read a feed.
here, the model being evaluated, as it answers a session. The person a pod is about is written "the person" on this page.
the first line of a job's prompt, `eval-tag: <run>/<job>`, by which a Workflow agent's transcript is known as the job's.
wording the scrubber cannot remove that could let a judge guess the arm, such as "the pod" or "line 211"; each is recorded with its arm and question.
codes, words, a day and a kind of record that the caller holds an absence to as well as the absence's own, passed as `tied`; the evals take them from their answer key.
a function a model may call: a name, a description, a JSON Schema for its input, and the code that runs it.
one run of a tool by a model: the tool's name, the input it was given, whether it succeeded, and what it returned.
the `.jsonl` file Claude Code writes of one session: every model call with its tokens, and every tool use.
a key item that names something a good answer does not say; it is graded avoided or raised, and counted apart from the key items an answer should find.
a W3C text format for writing statements in the vocabulary's terms; `pod.enter()` and `pod.judge()` take it.
here, what one judge wrote of one packet: a grade for each key item under each letter, and a grade for each point beyond the key.
one thing in a view, such as one medication or one lab result: the records that are one thing, shown as one. A row names it in `entry`, by an IRI that ends in `#` and 64 hexadecimal digits.
one tool use of a job outside what it was allowed: a file read, a command run or a file written that is not its own.
the jobs the runner starts together; the cap is checked between waves.
